clue.text: It was for Brutus in fashion to show temper

indicators.note: in says the Latin words sit inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a fashion is a mode
Brutus was a Roman, and in his Latin 'it was' is erat

explanation.surface: A remark about how Brutus showed his anger in a stylish way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was for Brutus' asks for the Latin, ERAT, placed inside MODE. 'Temper' is a verb here: to moderate is to tone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or restrain it, a synonym.

clue.text: Arkwright's son, upset, dismissed Big Toomai

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the son's name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Noah built the ark, and Ham was one of his sons
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Seems to concern the son of the inventor Richard Arkwright dismissing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright is not the inventor but Noah, the wright who built the ark. 'upset' turns HAM to MAH. Big Toomai is the elephant-driver in Kipling's 'Toomai of the Elephants'.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Toomai in Kipling's story is an elephant-keeper, an example of the job.

clue.text: France's one-time stage industry

explanation.surface: Sounds like a note about the hard work of the French theatre of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' is a stagecoach, not a theatre: the French public coach of former times had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The old French public stagecoach bore this name; the word also means hard-working application.

clue.text: Perform again, in classical thing for the screen

indicators.note: in says the word for performing again goes inside the Latin word

parts.note: res is Latin, the classical language, for thing
to perform again is to redo

explanation.surface: Instructions to restage something in a classical work for the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical' points to Latin: RES is 'thing'. REDO goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental partition behind a church altar, a kind of screen.

clue.text: Once a private sort of bar

explanation.surface: A note on a past soldier and a type of bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins was the old nickname for a British private soldier; a tommy bar is a short lever used to turn a box spanner.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical slang name for an ordinary British soldier, and the lever that turns a socket spanner.

clue.text: Old Persian governor has gin from South Africa

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A colonial official supposedly gets his gin from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a hunter's snare. The pieces go in answer order, SA first.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial rulers of the ancient Persian empire bore this title.

clue.text: Ammunition, Scots own up, is just gas

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the Scots word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: in Scots dialect 'ain' means own

explanation.surface: A claim that a Scottish munition is only gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AIN to NIA in this down clue. 'is just' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent colourless compound of nitrogen and hydrogen, which is a gas at room temperature.

clue.text: Eau de Cologne?

parts.note: read literally as French, 'water of Cologne', meaning the river that runs through that German city

explanation.definitionFit: The great German river that flows past Cologne, its literal water.

clue.text: Well and good for some people on a small income

indicators.note: for some means only some of the letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A phrase of approval for those on a modest wage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' signals letters taken from inside 'people on a small'. 'Well and good' is an example of using more words than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'well' and 'good' together is redundant phrasing, an example of the figure of speech.

clue.text: Anecdotes on them --'a curse!

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about other people's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of anecdotes, is a crossword staple; 'on' links it to THEM and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ecclesiastical curse or ban, a synonym.

clue.text: Governing body thrice improperly named, said Voltaire

definitions.text: Governing body thrice improperly named, said Voltaire

parts.words: Governing body thrice improperly named, said Voltaire
parts.note: Voltaire quipped that a certain medieval European realm was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire: three words in its title, each wrong

explanation.surface: A political entity whose name a French writer called wrong three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: Voltaire's famous jibe was that it was 'neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire', which is why each of the three words is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Central European realm Voltaire mocked as a misnomer in all three of its words.

clue.text: Gun, brandished, oddly disheartened the wicked

indicators.note: something brandished is waved about, so the letters of the weapon are jumbled
disheartened removes the heart, the central letter, of the word oddly

explanation.surface: Someone waving a gun strangely dismayed the evildoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brandished' scrambles GUN to UNG; 'disheartened' takes the middle D out of ODDLY, leaving ODLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Godless people are collectively called by this word, a synonym for sinners.

clue.text: Abbey we may visit — can a bird?

parts.note: a can is a tin
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A question whether a bird is allowed into the abbey we tour.
explanation.walkthrough: TINTERN Abbey is a famous ruined abbey in the Welsh Borders. 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruined Cistercian monastery in Monmouthshire, a well-known tourist site.

clue.text: Liqueur served incongruously in tea set

indicators.note: served in an odd, out-of-place way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A liqueur oddly poured into a tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served incongruously' rearranges the letters of IN TEA SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured sweet spirit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Song that's lachrymose? No, the dry version

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking if a song is tearful, then offering a dry alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges NO THE DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament or dirge, a tearful song mourning the dead.

clue.text: Return of spring is at perigee for instance

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word for spring is read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seemingly an astronomical note about spring returning at the closest point of an orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns SPA into APS. Perigee, the nearest point of an orbit to Earth, is one example of the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Perigee is one of the two extreme orbital points, which astronomy groups under this general term.

clue.text: Bird boy taken in

parts.note: a swallow is a bird
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad who has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' means deceived or believed: both senses of swallowed fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken in, like swallowing a story, means being fooled by it.

clue.text: Honourable .follower 'of Jean Paul in the race

indicators.note: follower of puts the abbreviation for honourable after the revolutionary's surname

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a French revolutionary

explanation.surface: A distinguished disciple of a man named Jean Paul takes part in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat, the French revolutionary murdered in his bath, gives MARAT; 'follower of' puts HON after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance running event of about 26 miles.

clue.text: Region round Napoleon's first battleground

indicators.note: round says the word for region encircles the letter

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Napoleon's name

explanation.surface: A district around the place of Napoleon's first battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives N, which 'round' puts inside AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest or combat, a synonym.

clue.text: The dog is under the log

definitions.text: The dog is under the log

parts.words: The dog is under the log
parts.note: the dog is a firedog, the metal stand that holds burning logs in a hearth

explanation.surface: A pet lying beneath a fallen tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal support in a fireplace holding wood above the hearth, also called a firedog.

clue.text: Step on stage again to prepare a new production

indicators.note: a new production remakes the material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor returning to the stage to rehearse a fresh show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production' rearranges PREPARE A.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view or onto the boards, a synonym for returning.

clue.text: Two about right — that's plain

indicators.note: about says the word for two goes round the letter

parts.note: two make a pair
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Two people discussing what is right, and that is plainly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' is the noun, flat grassland, not 'obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide treeless grassland of North America, a type of open lowland.

clue.text: Was he born perhaps where Sarah died?.

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man was born in the place where Sarah died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HE BORN. In Genesis, Abraham's wife Sarah died in Hebron.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis records the wife of Abraham dying in this town in Canaan.

clue.text: Musicians performing with careless freedom

parts.note: a group of musicians is a band, here 'a band'
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: Players giving a show with uninhibited liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as A BAND ON: a group of musicians that is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon as a noun means a lack of inhibition, a synonym.

clue.text: Saint 'a long time without name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the long time encloses the letter

parts.note: a long time is ages

explanation.surface: A holy person for ages without a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so AGES goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman virgin martyr venerated as a saint, an example.

clue.text: Baroness Nairne's. darling a fool?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a songwriter's beloved was an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Nairne wrote the Scottish Jacobite song 'Charlie is my darling'. Calling someone a 'right charlie' is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Prince Charles Edward Stuart is the darling of the song; in British slang the name also means a silly person.

clue.text: Many love' to embrace revolutionary belief

indicators.note: to embrace means the two letters hug the word for revolutionary between them

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
love is zero in tennis, O
a revolutionary is a red

explanation.surface: Lots of people adore a radical faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts RED between C and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed or statement of faith, a synonym.

clue.text: Secular struggle

parts.note: secular here means lasting a century, not worldly, so the struggle is a war counted in centuries

explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-French conflict of 1337-1453, named for its length of about a century.

clue.text: Parker thus making progress in detective work?

definitions.text: Parker thus making progress in detective work?

parts.words: Parker thus making progress in detective work?
parts.note: a nosy parker is a busybody; such a person advancing an inquiry would be prying with the nose

explanation.surface: A detective called Parker getting somewhere with a case.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nosy parker' is British for a meddlesome busybody, so Parker suggests the nose rather than a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking about inquisitively, as a busybody does when investigating.

clue.text: Attitude, I assume, of an, ancient god

parts.note: an attitude struck is a pose
taken as written
to assume clothes is to don them

explanation.surface: Describing the stance of an old deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' is in the sense of putting on clothes, DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of the sea, one of the old Olympian gods.
